title: Discovery of UMI-77 as a novel Ku70/80 inhibitor sensitizing cancer cells to DNA damaging agents in vitro and in vivo.
authors: Chen, Xuening; Chen, Changkun; Luo, Chengmiao; Liu, Jianyong; Lin, Zhonghui
one_liner_zh: 该文发现小分子抑制剂UMI-77靶向Ku70/80复合物并破坏其与DNA结合，涉及分子对接但核心是药物筛选与肿瘤增敏，非TF-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: The emergence of chemoresistance poses a significant challenge to the efficacy of DNA-damaging agents in cancer treatment, in part due to the inherent DNA repair capabilities of cancer cells. The Ku70/80 protein complex (Ku) plays a central role in double-strand breaks (DSBs) repair through the classical non-homologous end joining (c-NHEJ) pathway, and has proven to be one of the most promising drug target for cancer treatment when combined with radiotherapy or chemotherapy. In this study, we conducted a high-throughput screening of small-molecule inhibitors targeting the Ku complex by using a fluorescence polarization-based DNA binding assay. From a library of 11,745 small molecules, UMI-77 was identified as a potent Ku inhibitor, with an IC(50) value of 2.3 muM. Surface plasmon resonance and molecular docking analyses revealed that UMI-77 directly bound the inner side of Ku ring, thereby disrupting Ku binding with DNA. In addition, UMI-77 also displayed potent inhibition against MUS81-EME1, a key player in homologous recombination (HR), demonstrating its potential for blocking both NHEJ- and HR-mediated DSB repair pathways. Further cell-based studies showed that UMI-77 could impair bleomycin-induced DNA damage repair, and significantly sensitized multiple cancer cell lines to the DNA-damaging agents. Finally, in a mouse xenograft tumor model, UMI-77 significantly enhanced the chemotherapeutic efficacy of etoposide with little adverse physiological effects. Our work offers a new avenue to combat chemoresistance in cancer treatment, and suggests that UMI-77 could be further developed as a promising candidate in cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: 化疗耐药性的出现对DNA损伤药物在癌症治疗中的疗效构成了重大挑战，部分原因在于癌细胞固有的DNA修复能力。Ku70/80蛋白复合物（Ku）在通过经典非同源末端连接（c-NHEJ）途径修复双链断裂（DSBs）中发挥核心作用，并已被证明是与放疗或化疗联合使用时最有前景的癌症治疗药物靶点之一。在本研究中，我们利用基于荧光偏振的DNA结合实验，对靶向Ku复合物的小分子抑制剂进行了高通量筛选。从11,745个小分子库中，UMI-77被鉴定为一种强效Ku抑制剂，其IC(50)值为2.3 μM。表面等离子体共振和分子对接分析显示，UMI-77直接结合Ku环的内侧，从而干扰Ku与DNA的结合。此外，UMI-77还对MUS81-EME1表现出强效抑制作用，后者是同源重组（HR）中的关键因子，表明其具有阻断NHEJ和HR介导的DSB修复途径的潜力。进一步的细胞研究表明，UMI-77能损害博来霉素诱导的DNA损伤修复，并显著增强多种癌细胞系对DNA损伤药物的敏感性。最后，在小鼠异种移植肿瘤模型中，UMI-77显著增强了依托泊苷的化疗效果，且几乎没有不良生理影响。我们的工作为克服癌症治疗中的化疗耐药性提供了新途径，并表明UMI-77可进一步开发为癌症治疗的有前景候选药物。
